facts.claim: 2026 All-Star Game: three teams (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World) in a round robin of four 12-minute games; Game 1 Stars vs World, Game 2 Stripes vs Game-1 winner, Game 3 Stripes vs Game-1 loser, Game 4 championship between the top two; if all three finish 1-1 the first tiebreaker is point differential across each team's two games.
facts.verbatim_excerpt: Three teams (USA Stars, USA Stripes, and Team World) played a round-robin of four 12-minute games ... If all three teams finished 1-1, the NBA used point differential across each team's two round-robin games (WebSearch summary of the NBA release and CBS/Fox/NBC/Yahoo explainers); Kalshi KXNBAALLSTARGAME rules_secondary carries the same structure verbatim
facts.source_type: league release as summarised by WebSearch; Kalshi rules text (verbatim, in contract_rules_sample.json)

facts.claim: Game rules sheet: each game is one 12-minute period plus overtime if needed, no quarters and no displayed game clock; two 1:15 timeouts per team per game; one coach's challenge per game.
facts.verbatim_excerpt: each game had one 12-minute period plus overtime if needed, with no quarters and no game clock shown. Each team got two 1:15 timeouts per game ... and one coach's challenge per game (WebSearch summary of the official rules PDF; PDF not fetched)
facts.source_type: official rules PDF via search summary

facts.claim: Roster pool: 24 All-Stars chosen by vote (12 per conference; starters by fans/players/media, reserves by coaches); at least 16 US and 8 international players, Commissioner may add players; sources differ on the exact pool (25 voted plus three injury replacements) and Team World size (nine players per CBS).
facts.verbatim_excerpt: The NBA also required a minimum of 16 U.S. players and eight international players, with Commissioner Silver able to add players to reach those minimums. CBS reported that Team World had nine players. (WebSearch summary)
facts.source_type: secondary summary, sources differ on pool size

facts.claim: 2026 outcome: Stripes finished 2-0, Stars 1-1 (second seed), World 0-2 and eliminated; the championship was Stars 47, Stripes 21.
facts.verbatim_excerpt: The Stripes went 2-0 and the Stars went 1-1 ... The Stars then beat the Stripes in the final. ... USA Stars teammates over their fellow Americans on the Stripes team by a score of 47-21. (WebSearch summaries; Game 1 reported decided in overtime by a Scottie Barnes three)

facts.claim: 2026 All-Star MVP: Anthony Edwards (Kobe Bryant Trophy), 13 points in game 1, 11 in game 2, 8 in the final (32 across the tournament by the reported lines); reported as 10 of 14 votes with Kawhi Leonard (Stripes, a 31-point performance) receiving the other four; the panel votes right after the game and fans' votes make up 25% (secondary report; the media/fan split of the 14 votes is not given).
facts.verbatim_excerpt: Anthony Edwards won the 2026 All-Star Game MVP (the Kobe Bryant Trophy) with 10 of 14 votes, and Kawhi Leonard received the other four ... Fans also get a say, with their votes making up 25% of the total. (WebSearch summary)
facts.source_type: secondary; NBA MVP-selection description page not retrieved

facts.claim: 2026 Rising Stars: Carmelo Anthony, Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady each drafted a seven-player team; the fourth team (coach Austin Rivers) was G League Rising Stars; semifinals to 40, final to 25; Team Melo beat Team Austin 40-34, Team Vince beat Team T-Mac 41-36, final Team Vince 25-24 over Team Melo, MVP VJ Edgecombe (game-winning free throw).
facts.verbatim_excerpt: Each semifinal was won by the first team to reach or surpass 40 points, and the final by the first to reach or surpass 25. ... Team Vince edged Team Melo 25-24 in the championship game (WebSearch summary; semifinal and final scores each from a single outlet)
facts.source_type: secondary summary; targets also verbatim in Kalshi KXNBARISINGSTARS rules_secondary
